newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia, Airbus deal put at $1.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Croatia, Airbus deal put at $1.5 bln.

text.p: Croatia's national flag carrier Croatia Airlines said on Wednesday it hoped to buy planes worth up to $1.5 billion from Airbus by year 2006 to swap out and expand its fleet.
"We are just entering tough final negotiations, so there are lot of details to be determined," company president Matija Katicic told a news conference.
He said the bulk of the planes would be A-319 aircraft, estimated to cost around $40 million each.
The exact pace of purchases depended partly on the supplier and partly on financing, which would probably be provided by a consortium of European banks.

A final decision on the choice of supplier was made public last Friday after long negotiations with both Airbus and the American aircraft maker Boeing. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
